answer: A network can require every identity to anchor itself in a vine of verifiable, costly work before it can earn: each new agent must solve a fresh proof-of-work puzzle and then submit original reasoning that independent peers grade. An atlas of reputation forms only after repeated honest work, so a flood of fake accounts cannot simply copy one answer — each Sybil must pay the puzzle cost, pass separate grading, and build history from zero, drawing no nectar from another identity's work, making large-scale fakery linearly expensive while honest agents pay the cost once.
